The I/Os carry protection against high static voltages, but voltages above the maximum ratings should still be kept off them; unused inputs tied to a valid logic level improve reliability.

Up to four GPIOs set as 8-mA drivers may each sink loads of up to 18 mA, with VOL then specified at 1.2 V. No more than two such high-current outputs may sit on any one side of the package, and no more than four on the whole package.
Unless a table states otherwise, every timing figure is measured with the pin loaded by 50 pF to ground.

J2 is the TCK period, J3 and J4 its low and high halves, J5 and J6 its rise and fall. TMS and TDI are sampled on the rising edge of TCK (setup J7 and J9, hold J8 and J10). TDO changes on the falling edge of TCK: J11 from high impedance to valid data, J12 from one valid bit to the next, J13 from valid data back to high impedance.

VDDA is watched by a power-on reset (POR) monitor and a power-OK (POK) monitor. POR holds the analog circuits in reset until VDDA is high enough for them; POK holds the digital circuits in reset until VDDA reaches a working level. The digital power-on reset ends only when POR has released and every supply's POK monitor reports its rail in range. After that first release a dip on VDDA does not reassert the digital reset: it sets VDDARIS in RIS, and VDDAMIS in MISC when VDDAIM in IMC is set. VDDA rises over the time P1; POR releases at the P4 threshold, POK asserts at the P5 rising threshold and drops at the P5 falling threshold, which raises the interrupt.

Three monitors watch VDD: a power-OK (POK) and two brown-out detectors, BOR0 and BOR1. POK holds the digital circuits in reset until VDD reaches a working level, under the same release rule as VDDA. BOR0 and BOR1 either reset the device or raise an interrupt when VDD falls out of range; the BOR1 threshold lies between the BOR0 and POK thresholds. A BOR0 or BOR1 event sets BOR0RIS or BOR1RIS in RIS, BOR0MIS or BOR1MIS in MISC (when BOR0IM or BOR1IM in IMC is set), and the BOR bit in RESC when that event is set to cause a reset. BOR0IM and BOR1IM in IMC and the BOR0 and BOR1 bits in PBORCTL control both events. VDD rises over the time P2 and POK asserts at P6 rising; as VDD falls, BOR0 trips at P7, BOR1 at P8 and POK drops at P6 falling.

VDDC has one monitor, a power-OK (POK) that holds the digital circuits in reset until VDDC is in its working range, under the same release rule as the other supplies. VDDC rises over P3; POK asserts at the P9 rising threshold and drops at the P9 falling threshold.

Two tests show how short a VDD dip can be and still trip the BOR0, BOR1 and POR monitors. In the glitch test VDD falls linearly from 3.3 V to VDROP and returns at the same rate, tFALL = tRISE, over a total width tPW. In the droop test VDD falls from 3.3 V to VDROP in 10 ns, stays there, and returns in 10 ns, over a total width tPW. For each pulse width there is a VDROP at which each monitor responds.

The internal reset follows each reset source after a delay and then lasts for a set time. After the digital power-on reset it asserts within R1 and lasts R2; the digital power-on reset itself releases only once the analog POR has released and every supply's power-OK monitor is in range. After a brown-out it asserts within R3 and lasts R2. A low pulse on RST at least R4 long asserts it after R5, and it lasts R2. A software reset, a watchdog reset and a main-oscillator failure reset each hold the internal reset for R6, R7 and R8.

The listed crystals were simulated with this oscillator and confirmed to meet the main oscillator requirements; crystals with nearly the same parameters can be expected to work too. C0, C1 and L1 are typical motional figures from the crystal vendor, normally measured on a batch with a network analyzer; ESR, maximum drive level and CL are the vendor's maximums. The recommended C1 and C2 (pF) are the load capacitors on each crystal leg, and Rs (kΩ) is a resistor in series between OSC1 and the crystal that absorbs some power so the crystal's maximum drive level is not exceeded. These values belong with their own crystal only. WC Dl is the worst-case drive level found in simulation with them, which must not exceed the crystal's maximum; it also shows whether a similar crystal with a lower maximum drive level would do.

Every GPIO set as an input tolerates 5 V, except PD4, PD5, PB0 and PB1, which are limited to 3.6 V. With VDD present a 5-V input does no harm. Without VDD, an input in the 5 V ± 10% range is allowed over the device's lifetime for no more than 10,000 hours in total at 27 °C, or 5,000 hours at 85 °C; going past this affects reliability and the GPIO characteristics. An input in the 3.3 V ± 10% range without VDD, or in the 5 V ± 10% range with VDD, has no lifetime limit.

operation.topic: I/O pin types and ESD protection
operation.text: For ESD and leakage the pins fall into three groups: power pins; fail-safe pins, which are all GPIOs except PD4 and PD5; and non-fail-safe pins, which are PD4, PD5 and the other non-power, non-GPIO pins. The limits for power pins are those of the recommended operating conditions.

On the fail-safe GPIOs the ESD clamp sits between the pad and GND with no path from the pad to any supply rail, so an unpowered device cannot be powered through them. Their input voltage should stay within the absolute maximum ratings to keep leakage and injection current acceptable. Inside, a clamp limits the internal swing to VDD without limiting the pad; it starts to conduct once VIN is above VDD and below 4.5 V, drawing a larger but bounded current, so static inputs between VDD and 4.5 V cost power. PB0, PB1 and PE3, when used as inputs, need a strong external pull-up to stay above VIH min during power-on.

The main oscillator pins and PD4 and PD5 have ESD diodes from the pad to both VDD and GND, so a forward-biased diode can connect the pad to an internal rail. Their voltage and current must stay within the non-fail-safe pad limits, and the ADC external reference limits (ADC Electrical Characteristics) should also be kept to avoid gain error.

The source, VS with its impedance Zs (RS and CS), drives the pin. Inside, each analog input pad has a 5-V ESD clamp to GND only and leakage IL; the pads of all inputs then pass through RADC, the total equivalent input resistance up to the sampling node, to the shared sampling capacitance CADC of the 12-bit SAR converter, which delivers a 12-bit word. VADCIN is the voltage at the pin.

S1 is the SSIClk period, S2 and S3 its high and low times, S4 and S5 its rise and fall. In the TI synchronous serial frame format (FRF = 01), SSIFss pulses for one clock before each transfer of 4 to 16 bits, sent MSB first on SSITx and SSIRx. In the MICROWIRE format (FRF = 10), the master sends an 8-bit control word on SSITx, then after one idle bit (0) the slave returns 4 to 16 bits of data on SSIRx, MSB first, with SSIFss low through the frame. In the SPI format (FRF = 00) with SPH = 1 and either clock polarity (SPO = 0 or 1): as master, transmit data is valid within S6 of the clock edge and held S7, and receive data needs setup S8 and hold S9; as slave, transmit data is valid within S10 and held S11, and receive data needs setup S12 and hold S13.

After a start condition SCL stays high for I1 with SDA low; each SCL low period lasts at least I2 and each high period at least I6. Data is held I4 after SCL falls, becomes valid I10 after it, and is set up I7 before SCL rises. A repeated start needs I8 of setup, and a stop condition I9. I3 and I5 are the rise and fall times of SCL and SDA.

The DID0 register's MAJOR and MINOR fields also give the revision.

circuits.description: RST pulled up to VDD so the part relies on its internal power-on reset alone. The pull-up may be anything from 0 to 100 kΩ, 0 meaning RST tied straight to VDD.

circuits.title: External circuitry to extend power-on reset
circuits.description: An RC network on RST: R1 pulls RST up to VDD and C1 holds it low for a while after power is applied, delaying the end of reset and filtering noise on the pin.

circuits.description: A push-button reset. R1 and C1 set the power-on delay on RST; pressing SW1 pulls RST to ground through R2.
